notable_anecdotes: CJ's autobiographical credential as the LP's chief legal counsel after Edsa under Senate President Jovito R. Salonga -- making the Robredo-as-independent critique a personally-informed institutional judgment rather than partisan commentary, and tying this column back to D21 and C17 as part of the Salonga personal-lineage thread.
The Sharon-Pangilinan family detail -- '(to his wife Sharon's comfort)' -- preserving Kiko Pangilinan's withdrawal-willingness with a quietly affectionate parenthetical reference to Sharon Cuneta.

Mocha Uson's 2016 Duterte campaign metrics -- 4 million likes, 1.2 million engagements -- preserved from the ISEAS-Yusof Ishak Institute's 2020 white paper as the social-media benchmark Robredo's 'kakampinks' must match.

CJ's specific reading recommendation -- Damon Centola's 'Change' (January 2021) on 'strength of weak ties' and 'weakness of strong ties' -- a rare CJ-as-strategist book-recommendation moment in his political-analysis columns.
The Imee 'dream team' framing reference -- embedding the Marcos-sibling network into the 2022 strategy without naming it as scheme.

Bongbong's KBL-avoidance fact -- 'has chosen to run under the little-known Federal Party and not under the tarnished KBL of martial law vintage' -- among CJ's most explicit references to martial-law era branding in his 2022-election analysis.
The 'no independent has ever been elected president' line -- categorical historical-precedent statement deployed against Robredo's strategic choice.

The Isko Moreno 'Healing President' positioning -- 'canny adoption of the good policies and projects of President Duterte and of former president Ferdinand Marcos, and the rejection of their dubious ones' -- one of CJ's most concise characterizations of Moreno's reconciliation pitch.
The 'Yorme's Akyon Demokratiko' Tagalog-loanword usage (Yorme being a syllable-reversal Filipino term for Mayor) -- preserving Manila political vernacular in the column.

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban frames the 2022 election around a single deadline-anchored pivot: on or before November 15, Mayor Sara Duterte must decide with finality whether to substitute for Sen. Bato dela Rosa as the PDP-Laban / Lakas-CMD presidential bet. Though the 'feisty Inday' has steadfastly refused any national post, CJ would not be surprised if her teeming supporters flood streets, rallies, and social media with 'Run, Sara, Run.' If she relents, she gets ample logistics, slate-selection privileges, and an 'enviable problem' of donation-management; if she refuses, candidates will scramble for administration blessing -- and 'past elections have shown that the administration can shepherd up to 10 percent of the votes,' decisive in tight multiparty contests. Manila Mayor Isko Moreno would probably be the big beneficiary of an Inday cop-out via his 'canny' 'Healing President' positioning -- pandemic critic AND adopter of 'good policies and projects' of Duterte and Marcos, with rejection of dubious ones -- and may even win Solid North blessings by convincing Bongbong Marcos to substitute for Willie Ong as his running mate. Alternatively, Bongbong may join PDP-Laban to actualize Imee Marcos's 'dream team' of Sara-Bongbong (he already chose the little-known Federal Party over 'the tarnished KBL of martial law vintage'). Sen. Ping Lacson, stuck in the Pulse Asia 'cellar,' may have to bite the bullet and save his partner Sen. Tito Sotto a slot elsewhere -- Akyon Demokratiko (Yorme), Promdi (Pacquiao), PDP-Laban, or even the Liberal Party, where VP bet Sen. Kiko Pangilinan has publicly stated willingness (to his wife Sharon's comfort) to withdraw if it enhances Robredo. VP Leni Robredo will remain the opposition's 'hallowed candidate' especially of the anti-Duterte and anti-Marcos crowd, but if Sara runs, Leni loses her 'only lady' distinction -- and her strange choice to run as independent (not as LP nominee, despite chairing the LP) deprives her of the LP's dominant-minority-party legal pluses and 'an army of loyal cadres down to the barangay level' from a 75-year-old party (CJ knows this from his own post-Edsa role as LP chief legal counsel under Senate President Jovito R. Salonga). And 'no independent has ever been elected president.' The pandemic-driven online campaign shift raises crucial questions for Robredo: do her 'kakampinks' have the expertise to match Mocha Uson's 2016 Duterte campaign (4 million likes, 1.2 million engagements per ISEAS-Yusof Ishak's 2020 white paper), and her team should read Damon Centola's 'Change' (January 2021) on 'strength of weak ties' and 'weakness of strong ties' in spreading beliefs to avoid preaching to the converted. In sum, whether she runs or not, 'Sara will be the game changer of the political landscape come Nov. 15.'
